newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Higher yields coming up for Belgian OLOs.
newsitem.headline: Higher yields coming up for Belgian OLOs.

text.p: Belgian linear bonds extended Tuesday's correction on Wednesday afternoon but the slip would pale in comparison with a bigger slide in the second half of the year, traders said.
At 1330 GMT, the benchmark 2007 OLO was yielding 5.82 percent against 5.80 on Tuesday and 5.75 on Monday.

Analyst Conrad Fieremans predicted, before the weakening in mid afternoon, that chart-technically -- based on the key day reversal -- OLOs had some immediate downward potential but that fundamentals indicated it would only be modest and that a trend reversal was ruled out for now.
Fieremans said he saw higher levels for yields after the summer, taking into acccount a recovery of the economy in Europe.
He expected yields of between 6.00 percent for Bunds and 6.00 to 6.10 percent for OLOs.
One dealer said the outcome of the EU summit in Amsterdam had been less than impressive but had nevertheless weighed on volumes in recent days.
The next target would be the Group of Seven meeting in Denver, Colorado, on June 20-22, he said.
"In between those two events, it's no man's land," he said.
Fieremans said that the inflation picture in the U.S. was still favourable, making it unlikely the Federal Reserve would hike interest rates in two weeks time.
Traders expected the yield spread between 10-year OLOs and Bunds to remain locked in the five to 10 basis points range. It was at eight on Wednesday.
Fieremans said he expected the negative spread in France to disappear gradually. Speculation would be aimed at the spread in Italy and, to a lesser extent, Spain.
He believed that the upcoming summer months would not be a stable period.
"Not really, with such low volumes, movements might be quite big," he said.
